answer: A sybil farm survives by spreading clones over many cheap keys, so resistance should tax correlation, not headcount. The summit of this design is a random witness rotation: each close, a fixed-size panel is drawn per answer, so a farm cannot predict which of its clones will judge a given tx. A pearl of a check is a correlated stake freeze: identities linked by shared funding or overlapping hardware fingerprints have a portion frozen until their joint attestations diverge. At the nadir of the attack, cost scales per cluster, not per key.
